output.summary: KEP-962 proposed ExecutionHook, a namespaced API plus an ExecutionHookController, to trigger user commands in pods/containers on demand (e.g., quiesce/unquiesce around volume snapshots). Its status is implementable, stage alpha.
output.rationale: Volume snapshots do not guarantee application consistency, so users must quiesce applications manually before and after a snapshot. The existing container lifecycle hooks run only at container start or termination, so the KEP proposes hooks triggered on demand, with a HookAction object to share command definitions. The controller runs the hook and updates its status, and garbage-collects hook objects per a policy.

alternatives.option: Use annotations to define the execution hook when it is not in the container struct
alternatives.why_not: Listed only as an alternative in the readme; the sources do not give a further reason it was not chosen.

alternatives.option: Alternative designs discussed in design meetings and spec reviews
alternatives.why_not: Comments say the project needed a redesign after review comments, and that the team planned a different approach in issue 1977, but the sources do not detail the alternatives' tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: The lifecycle hook is called immediately after a container is created or immediately before a container is terminated.
The proposed execution hook is not tied to the start or termination time of the container. It can be triggered on demand by callers (users or controllers)
The plan is to go with a different approach as described here: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1977. If that goes through, we won't need this one any more.
We actually need to do some re-design on this. So we won't track this for 1.19 yet.
The KEP is merged (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-storage/20190120-execution-hook-design.md) but implementation is WIP.
